# Binary numbers (`binary_numbers`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/computing.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Computing, control & information theory (`computing`)
- Deps: needs zero_place_value; helped by arabic_numerals
- Core idea: Any number can be written with only two digits, 0 and 1, if each place is worth twice the one to its right (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and so on) instead of ten times: thirteen is 1101, that is 8 + 4 + 0 + 1. Arithmetic becomes trivial: the whole addition table is 0+0=0, 0+1=1, 1+1=10, and multiplication is only shifting and adding. The price is length, a little more than three binary digits for each decimal digit. Since a digit has only two values, anything with two states can hold it: a hole or no hole, a switch open or closed, a current on or off, which is why calculating machines built from switches use binary.
- Pitfalls:
  - Reading 10 as ten; in binary it is two
  - Proposing binary for human bookkeeping; its value lies in machines, for people it is only longer
  - Claiming the I Ching contains binary arithmetic; the hexagrams are two-valued patterns, and Leibniz read his own system into them in 1701–1703
  - Confusing binary numbers with a code such as Morse, which uses more than two signal elements
- History: egypt: c. 1550 BC – multiplication by repeated doubling (Rhind papyrus) uses the binary decomposition of a number implicitly; india: c. 3rd–2nd c. BC (date uncertain) – Pingala's Chandahsastra enumerates metres of long and short syllables in a binary scheme; china: c. 9th c. BC onwards – the 64 hexagrams of the I Ching; 11th c. Shao Yong arranges them in what is in effect binary counting order, without arithmetic; europe: c. 1604 – Harriot's unpublished binary arithmetic; 1670 Caramuel; 1679 Leibniz writes a manuscript on binary arithmetic. His separate Explication de l'arithmétique binaire is presented in 1703 and printed in 1705; americas: 1937 – Stibitz's relay adder at Bell Labs; 1945 von Neumann's EDVAC report settles on binary for electronic computers
- Read:
  - G. W. Leibniz, Explication de l'arithmétique binaire, Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences for 1703 (printed 1705)
  - Lloyd Strickland & Harry Lewis, Leibniz on Binary: The Invention of Computer Arithmetic (2022)
